sections.content:
7,555 people

were counted on the census as "exam invigilators" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the fourth most common occupation reported on the census.

Exam invigilators set up, run and invigilate exams to ensure exams are conducted in line with the relevant regulations.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "exam invigilators" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "exam invigilators", 28.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "exam invigilators" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "exam invigilators" included:

  • bed and breakfast and guest house owners and proprietors
  • care escorts
  • elected officers and representatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "exam invigilators" there were more women than men (76.9% compared with 23.1%).

This means "exam invigilators" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 23.1% and women made up 76.9% of "exam invigilators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "exam invigilators" included:

  • other educational professionals
  • social services managers and directors
  • library clerks and assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "exam invigilators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged between 30 and 49 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "exam invigilators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "exam invigilators", 14.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (94.6% compared with 5.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.7%) than self-employed (6.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
